indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the rustic word goes round the number

parts.note: a peasant is a rural labourer
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A friendly rustic of about fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like an approximate age but tells you to put L inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affable is easy-going and agreeable, which is to say nice to be with.

explanation.surface: Enjoying a tricky spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a preserved condiment such as chutney, and a predicament or fix is also called by the same word.

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, superior
a cross-reference to the 1 Across answer, which means agreeable

explanation.surface: A girl gets together with an upper-class Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'l' is the figure 1: 1 Across is PLEASANT, here standing for its synonym. U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, from the Greek for good victory.

clue.text: Under-cover directions given in a letter

indicators.note: given in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a screed is a long piece of writing, such as a lengthy letter
N and E are the compass directions north and east

explanation.surface: Secret instructions passed on in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a letter' suggests one character of the alphabet, but it is a long letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden from view behind a shield or partition, so concealed.

clue.text: A famous school set up this record

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A renowned school established this record.
explanation.definitionFit: To jot something down is to make a record of it.

clue.text: Stout fellow employed as a caretaker

explanation.surface: A heavy man takes a job looking after a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout is a dark beer also called by this name, and a doorkeeper or caretaker of a building is likewise so called.

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very large
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A huge duck that is all skin and bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or made of bone, the anatomical adjective.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the current word goes round the letter

parts.note: topical means current, of present interest

explanation.surface: Hot news, as current as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hot regions near the equator, so the adjective means sweltering.

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Accounting for growth in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An account or narration of events, as in the relation of a story.

parts.note: to con is to swindle or cheat
trite means stale or hackneyed

explanation.surface: A swindler, exhausted, is wracked by guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling guilt-ridden is being penitent, sorry for a wrong done.

parts.note: a ship heels or rolls when it tips to one side

explanation.surface: Taking a dog out along the road, with the command to heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' suggests a dog or a shoe, but here it is the nautical sense of leaning over, as a ship rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk is a gentle saunter.

explanation.surface: A poet is not one to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender was an English poet of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was a British poet, and someone who lays out money freely is the opposite of a miser.

explanation.surface: A dog barked, though it was cowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gave tongue can mean applied the tongue, lapped; and to be beaten or overcome is to be thrashed in the slang sense.

clue.text: He always expects to get a buzz at his place of work

definitions.text: He always expects to get a buzz at his place of work

parts.words: He always expects to get a buzz at his place of work
parts.note: a buzz sounds like excitement from the job, but this worker literally hears bees buzzing among his hives

explanation.surface: A man who always finds his job thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper tends hives full of humming insects every working day.

indicators.note: something defective needs fixing, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A broken foot pedal needs replacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Modified or made different.

clue.text: Giving a hand to many exceptionally genial characters

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, so a large number

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Lending a helping hand to lots of unusually friendly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges GENIAL into EALING after D; 'characters' just tells you the letters are used. 'Giving a hand' is the card-game sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In cards, the dealer distributes a hand to each player.

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop down
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Pop over to get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' reads as a visit, but splits into SAG and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A starch from palm pith, used in milk puddings.

parts.note: a dog show winner is suggested, but these gundogs show where game is by standing rigid and aiming their noses

explanation.surface: Dogs doing well at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Gundogs bred to indicate the position of game by freezing with the nose aimed.

clue.text: The board put on weight, due to copious seafood

parts.note: a plank is a board of wood
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: The committee gained weight from eating a lot of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The board' looks like a committee but is a wooden plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting microscopic organisms in vast numbers are food for whales and fish.

clue.text: Fit means used, that's quite clear

indicators.note: used here means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fit means were used, that is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain to see, evident.

clue.text: Not all who slog hard build up capital

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not everyone who works hard ends up wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'hard build up', which means nothing for a city; only 'capital' defines, the rest is surface. 'capital' pretends to be money.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of Norway's government.

indicators.note: behind places the letter after the other piece

parts.note: genera are kinds or classes, plural of genus

explanation.surface: Ordinary types are left at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common is widespread, applying to most rather than a few.

clue.text: A goddess writing one note after another

parts.note: A is a musical note
then means afterwards
another note, E

explanation.surface: A goddess composing music note by note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' is a link; 'another' means a further note, E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek patron of Athens, deity of wisdom.

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people at church display courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; 'pluck' suggests courage but means grab.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck is to grab or seize something quickly.

clue.text: Debtor needs right backing in ruination

explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses TORY into YROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal decay of timber that brings wooden buildings to ruin.

clue.text: A number of bonds for one's old age?

parts.note: nine is a number
ties are bonds or links

explanation.surface: Saving up bonds for one's retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonds' suggests investments for old age; the definition is playful, the decade a person reaches in very old age.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in their tenth decade of life, from ninety upwards, is very elderly.

clue.text: A fixer in the London suburbs

explanation.surface: A handyman working in outer London.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fastens with a pin is a fixer, and the place is a suburb in the London borough of Harrow.

clue.text: To create a disturbance could mean jail

explanation.surface: Causing trouble could land you in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate or provoke trouble, and slang for prison.

clue.text: Alternatively take it in here for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair is reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Or else, take it to her to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repair' rearranges IT and HERE; 'take' and 'in' are links. The held text reads 'her', an OCR slip for 'here'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, the word means also or as an alternative, as in 'I don't like it either'.

clue.text: Attending the big match or he'll swear!

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a Test is an international cricket match
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spectator at a major sporting fixture who might curse out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international fixture in cricket. 'swear' sounds like cursing, but it means giving sworn evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness who formally affirms or vouches for something under oath.

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Publish ten fresh lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourteen-line poem is a set of verse lines.

explanation.surface: Do you feel like hearing a tune?
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a whim or peculiar notion, and in notation a quarter note is a short musical symbol.
